title: McKinnon on why he scanned US military networks

tellings.quote: I read the disclosure project book Steven Greer and his team.

I thought I could use my basic networking skills just to do a scan, you know, a light scan on American military networks, which which is mad now, but but back then it was just kind of like a playful idea.
tellings.difference: Adds the method (blank passwords, a light scan) and the place (his girlfriend's aunt's house in London), and dates it 2000-2002.
tellings.link_reason: McKinnon scanning US military networks after reading the Disclosure Project book. This is the same account as the story about why he scanned those networks.

plain: A British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon says that after reading the book of the Disclosure Project, a group led by Steven Greer that gathered testimony about UFO secrecy, he decided to use his "basic networking skills" to do "a light scan on American military networks," which he calls "mad now" but then "a playful idea." He tells Michels he did it himself, from his girlfriend's aunt's house in London, using blank passwords, around 2000 to 2003 by his various datings, and that he got into the NSA at Fort Meade, the Defense Information Systems Agency, and Pentagon, Army, Navy and Air Force networks. He tells it to explain that he went in looking for the hidden UFO evidence the book described.
